request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A rate can now carry a to-date, and `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it behaves**
- **Which rate applies:** the rate with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date still applies, unless that date is after the rate's to-date. In that case the due is n/a. An earlier open-ended rate doesn't take over. The rule lives in one place on the server (`Rate.inForce`, used by claims, rollups and statements) and in `rateOn` on the front end, so the "in force today" rate column follows it too.
- **What follows from n/a:** totals skip an n/a claim, a statement binds n/a, and the late charge adds nothing to it.
- **Saving a rate:** the form has a new optional To field (`rate-form-to`), and each rate row shows it (`rate-to`). A to-date before the from-date is refused twice over: the form shows `rate-form-error`, and the server rejects it with a validation check, so nothing is stored or audited.
- **Audit:** `RATE_SET` gets ` to=<date>` at the end when a to-date was given.
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V31__rate_to_date.sql`, adds a `to_date` column to the rate table. Setting the same grade and from-date again replaces the to-date as well, and clears it if none was given.

**One change to existing behaviour:** the test needed one other rule changed. A person's due-total used to be n/a whenever no rate was in force today for their grades, unless a settled or stated claim kept a figure. Now any claim with a due also keeps it. Without this, a person whose claims were all dated inside a rate that has since ended would show n/a instead of their total; the test expects 3.00 here. A person with no claims with a due still shows n/a. I changed it in the same way in the server rollup, in the statement, and in the people screen.

Before to-dates this only differs in an unusual case: a claim dated after today, under a rate that starts after today.
